Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
XZealot wrote:
> Kushiel wrote:
> > Just want to check before I get all crazy with the diablerie.
> >
> > There's no set timing on the "burn this card to cancel a blood hunt on
> > a Brujah antitribu" clause of this card, correct?

You have to use it after the referendum passes and before the vampire
is burned by the blood hunt.

> > So I can wait and see
> > if it looks like the !Brujah is going to be burned before burning the
> > Dogs?

Yes, and ony then.

> Another question, do you burn Dogs of War out of you hand, or do you
> burn Dogs of War once it passes the vote and is on the table. Or, can
> you burn it under both conditions to cancel a bloodhunt?

You cannot merely discard it from your hand to cancel a blood hunt.
Once it is in play, you may burn it to cancel a blood hunt.

Messages.Author: Salem
Messages.Body:


A common misconception is that the referendum _is_ the bloodhunt. This
is not so. A referendum is called, and if it passes, there is a
bloodhunt on the vampire, which burns it.

So anything that cancels a bloodhunt can only do so after the referendum
has been called, and is found to be successful. Because before that time
there is no bloodhunt to cancel.

See page 44 of the 3rd Ed Rulebook. (6.5.6)

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:


It is so with effects that cancel a blood hunt, subject to other card
text.
Card text of "blood hunt" means the blood hunt.
Card text of "blood hunt referendum" or similar is used to refer to the
blood hunt referendum.
